newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: France not seeking to reopen EMU pact - Strauss-Kahn.
newsitem.headline: France not seeking to reopen EMU pact - Strauss-Kahn.

text.p: French Finance Minister Dominique Strauss-Kahn said on Monday that a meeting of European Union finance ministers had been unable to agree final details of a stability pact aimed at ensuring spending discipline among countries inside monetary union.
"We're not seeking to renegotiate the stability pact, but we cannot approve it today," Strauss-Kahn told a news conference.
He said budgetary discipline and price controls were essential, but Europe must not limit itself to this. It must focus on jobs and growth, he added.
Strauss-Kahn noted there would be further discussions with France's EU partners in the coming days, notably at a Franco-German summit in Poitiers in western France on Friday.
But asked whether he thought the EU could complete talks on the stability pact in time for a summit in Amsterdam on June 16-17, he said: "I don't believe we can complete it between now and then."
He noted that French Prime Minister Lionel Jospin was not due to make his keynote policy speech to parliament until June 19.
Strauss-Kahn also said there was no reason for financial markets to be worried. "The French government is totally determined to launch EMU on the planned (January 1, 1999) date," he said.
The Amsterdam summit had been expected to approve the pact which was largely agreed by EU leaders at a Dublin summit last December.
